name: copy-standards

description: >-
  Standards for the copy kind — self-contained pieces read start to finish: essays, articles, long-form landing-page narrative. Reference skill loaded by the composed copy skills, not invoked directly.

---

<objective>
The copy kind's standards layer over `/prose-standards` — inherited rules, no overrides, and the composition rules for self-contained pieces.
</objective>

<reference_note>
This is a reference skill. `/author-copy` and `/audit-copy` load it; the routers reach it only through them.
</reference_note>

<inherited_rules>
Every `/prose-standards` anti-pattern applies unchanged, at zero tolerance — word choice (significance and authenticity adverbs, overused vocabulary, ornate nouns, pompous verbs), sentence structure (negative parallelism, stacked negations, rhetorical self-answers, anaphora and tricolon abuse, filler transitions, tacked-on significance, false ranges, gerund fragment litanies, tautological definitions, redundant paired examples), paragraph structure (punchy-fragment paragraphs, listicles in a trench coat), tone (false suspense, unnecessary metaphors, hypothetical openers, performed vulnerability, asserted clarity, stakes inflation, condescension, vague attributions, invented concept labels), formatting (em-dash overuse, bold-first bullets, unicode decoration), and composition (fractal summaries, dead metaphors, analogy stacking, one-point dilution, duplication, signposted conclusions, dismissive optimism). Composing skills load `/prose-standards` for the full descriptions and examples.
</inherited_rules>

<overrides>
None. Copy relaxes no base rule — the voice is the base voice.
</overrides>

<additional_rules>
Rules specific to self-contained pieces.

One voice, its own composition. Copy differs from the other kinds in composition only: argument structure, narrative arc, and development. Word- and sentence-level rules are the base catalog's.

Arguments progress. Each paragraph moves the piece forward — developing, supporting, or transitioning. A paragraph that could swap places with an earlier one without the reader noticing is redundant.

One developed example beats a stack. An example with real detail carries an argument; four examples at a sentence each substitute name-dropping for analysis. Develop each example that adds distinct information; cut the rest.

Rhetorical devices are single-use. One metaphor introduced, used, and released. One rule-of-three at the moment of payoff. A device that returns asks the reader to admire the writing instead of following the argument.

Length matches substance. A piece with one core insight is short. Word count tracks new information and reasoning, not the thesis's importance. A draft restating its core point more than twice is too long.

Endings end. The piece stops when the last new idea is complete — no summary ritual, no announced conclusion.

Tradeoffs live in place. Real difficulties appear in the section where they are relevant, with the same specificity and sourcing as any other claim — never as a bookend concession.
</additional_rules>

<success_criteria>
Copy meets this layer when every base anti-pattern is absent, each paragraph advances the piece, examples are developed rather than stacked, no rhetorical device recurs, and the piece ends without announcing it — and the catalog itself is sound: every additional rule above states a test a reader can apply to a draft.
</success_criteria>
